Expedia Sinks 12% as Soft Q4 Outlook Overshadows a Beat and Raise: JPMorgan Sees "Transitory" Slowdown ©@Tero Vesalainen from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Expedia shares fell 12% today after it forecast fourth-quarter revenue growth of 4.0%-5.7%, down from 12% in the third quarter.

Its fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA outlook is roughly flat with a year ago.

Marriott raised its full-year outlook this week, and Airbnb's next report should show whether the slowdown is Expedia's alone.

JPMorgan calls the slowdown "transitory," and the stock already traded below its five-year average forward P/E.

Expedia Group (EXPE:NASDAQ) beat its own guidance and raised its full-year outlook after Wednesday's close. The stock is down 12% today anyway.

Expedia expects fourth-quarter revenue of $3.69-$3.75 billion, growth of 4.0%-5.7%. That raises a question for Airbnb (ABNB:NASDAQ), which competes with Expedia's Vrbo, and for Marriott International (MAR:NASDAQ), which supplies many of the rooms Expedia sells.

A strong quarter, then a slow one

Third-quarter revenue grew 12% to $4.94 billion, and the full-year outlook rose to $16.37-$16.43 billion. Before the report, analysts expected $16.2 billion this year and $17.4 billion in 2027, about 7% growth:

Expedia Group (EXPE): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

The new outlook beats this year's estimate. But a fourth quarter growing 4.0%-5.7% is a slow lead-in to a 2027 that needs 7%. I'd expect that estimate to come down unless the slowdown fades quickly.

Profit looks weaker still: Expedia expects fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of $830-$880 million, against $848 million a year ago. On Wednesday's call, finance chief Derek Andersen blamed the US midterms and unrest in Europe and the Middle East.

TIKR tracks 38 analysts on Expedia Group. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Expedia Group, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Expedia Group's Analyst Ratings

Marriott isn't seeing it yet

Marriott's third quarter, reported Monday, shows no travel slump. RevPAR rose 6.5% worldwide and 4.4% internationally, and Marriott raised its full-year RevPAR outlook to 4.5%-5% growth. On the Middle East, CEO Anthony Capuano said "trends improved meaningfully from the second quarter." If Expedia's worries are right, Marriott's fourth quarter should cool too.

Airbnb's nights and seats booked grew 10% in the second quarter, faster than in the first. Expedia's consumer bookings, Vrbo included, grew 7% in the third quarter. If Airbnb's outlook holds up, the slowdown looks like Expedia's own.

Cheaper than usual

JPMorgan cut its target to $315 from $330 and kept its Neutral rating, calling the growth slowdown "transitory."

Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) reached a significant support level, and could be a good pick for investors from a technical perspective. Recently, ABNB broke through the 20-day moving average, which suggests a short-term bullish trend.

The 20-day simple moving average is a popular trading tool. It provides a look back at a stock's price over a 20-day period, and is beneficial to short-term traders since it smooths out price fluctuations and provides more trend reversal signals than longer-term moving averages.

The 20-day moving average can show signals that are similar to other SMAs as well. If a stock's price is moving above the 20-day, the trend is considered positive. When the price falls below the moving average, it can signal a downward trend.

5 Things Investors Need to Know About Thursday’s Markets

Stocks rocked higher in post-election trading Wednesday.
Credit: Michael Nagle / Bloomberg via Getty Images

Stock futures are pointing toward a mixed opening on Thursday, with futures tied to the S&P 500 faintly higher and those associated with Nasdaq 100 looking downward; the Dow looks like it could extend recent gains; Toyota shares are rising after the automaker lifted its outlook; AppLovin and Dutch Bros' shares are making relatively big moves, albeit in opposite directions; and investors are preparing for quarterly results from Airbnb and Cloudflare.

Here's what you need to know today.

Stock Futures Look Mixed

Stock futures looked mixed ahead of the opening bell after yesterday's big, and broad, post-election rally. Futures tied to the Dow were up about 0.7%, those tied to the S&P 500 were up 0.1%, and those associated with the tech-focused Nasdaq 100 were down some 0.8%.

Oil prices were rising, with Brent crude—the global oil benchmark—up about 3% to almost $98 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate—the U.S. benchmark—up some 2.5% to near $90 a barrel. The yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury notes was close to 4.89%, where it stood last night. The price of precious metals was increasing, as was bitcoin, which was recently trading for more than $79,600, according to CoinDesk.

Read today's full markets roundup here.

Dow Looks Poised for More Gains

The Dow appeared poised to climb again, with futures tied to the blue-chip index pointing higher. The Dow jumped 1,569 points, or 3%, on Wednesday, marking the index's fifth-largest one-day increase. All but three companies in the index logged gains yesterday with members like 3M (MMM), Microsoft (MSFT), Sherwin-Williams (SHW), McDonald's (MCD), Home Depot (HD) and Amazon (AMZN) all rising more than 5%. Tech isn't as widely represented in the Dow as in some other indexes, which may be making the Dow more attractive to investors who want to reduce their exposure to AI.

Toyota Shares Take Off on Brighter Outlook

A big Japanese carmaker's shares are driving higher this morning. Toyota's (TM) stock was recently up some 9% in U.S. trading as the company reported falling profits, but lifted its full-year outlook. (They rose more than 16% in Japan.) Toyota's latest quarterly net income fell nearly 19% year-over-year to 759.4 billion yen as the manufacturer grappled with rising supply costs and U.S. tariffs, according to the company. Still, Toyota now expects 3.57 trillion yen in profit, up from 3.25 trillion yen in prior estimates.

AppLovin, Dutch Bros' Shares Are Big Morning Movers

Digital advertising company AppLovin (APP) and coffee chain Dutch Bros (BROS) were among the morning's biggest premarket movers. AppLovin shares were recently up some 22% after the company reported a 72% year-over-year jump in profit and record revenue on Wednesday. Dutch Bros' shares were off more than 11% after the drive-thru chain published a muted forecast with its quarterly results on Wednesday. Dutch Bros' full-year forecast of "at least $2.1 billion" matched the $2.13 billion expected, according to Visible Alpha's survey of analysts. Slower sales may have investors worried about inflation-weary consumers cutting back—a concern that has dogged rivals like Starbucks and other quick-service restaurants.

(Updates with economic data, recent oil price movement, world markets' overview and corporate stock movements.)

US equity futures were mixed pre-bell Thursday as traders observed artificial intelligence and data center-related stocks slipping after the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were 0.6% higher, S&P 500 futures were up 0.1%, and Nasdaq futures were 0.8% lower.

Investors are concerned that the Democratic control of Congress could bring heightened scrutiny of the data-center industry and potentially slow its development. Banks are also preparing for more oversight, with lawmakers seen probing consumer finance practices that could potentially increase customer costs, according to Reuters.

Traders also digested the latest round of earnings, with ConocoPhillips (COP) posting higher Q3 adjusted earnings and revenue, and Sony Group (SONY) reporting higher fiscal Q2 earnings and sales.

Monster Beverage (MNST) and Airbnb (ABNB) are expected to report their Q3 earnings after the market closes.

Oil prices were higher, with front-month global benchmark North Sea Brent crude up 2.2% at $96.71 per barrel and US West Texas Intermediate crude 1.4% higher at $89.32 per barrel.

Initial jobless claims dropped to 189,000 in the week ended Oct. 31 from an upwardly revised 195,000 level in the previous week, compared with expectations for an increase to 196,000 in a survey compiled by Bloomberg.

Q3 nonfarm productivity increased at a 3.6% annual rate compared with the 2.7% gain expected, while unit labor costs declined 1.2%, compared with the 0.4% gain expected.

Federal Reserve Cleveland President Beth Hammack, Richmond President Thomas Barkin and Dallas President Lorie Logan are the Fed speakers for Thursday.

In other world markets, Japan's Nikkei closed 1.8% lower, Hong Kong's Hang Seng ended 3.7% higher, and China's Shanghai Composite finished 0.1% higher. Meanwhile, the UK's FTSE 100 was up 0.8%, and Germany's DAX index was 0.6% higher in Europe's early afternoon session.

In equities, neocloud stocks declined amid worries about the potential backlash against AI and data centers, with Nebius Group (NBIS) falling 4.3% and CoreWeave (CRWV) dipping 4.1% in premarket trading. Qualcomm (QCOM) shares dropped more than 11% after the company reported lower fiscal Q4 adjusted earnings and revenue late Wednesday.

On the winning side, stocks of ConocoPhillips and Sony were up 1.8% and 6.1%, respectively, after the companies posted their quarterly financial results. Toyota Motor (TM) shares rose 8.1% after the company reported higher Q2 sales revenue and boosted its fiscal 2027 EPS outlook.

DraftKings, Novavax, GoPro, Tapestry, Airbnb, and Akamai will report earnings on Thursday, while economic data releases include weekly jobless claims and Friday's October nonfarm payrolls report.

U.S. equity futures were mixed early on Thursday after the previous session's rally, helped by a sharp drop in oil prices and greater clarity following Democrats' midterm victories.

As of 3.45 a.m. ET, S&P 500 futures fell 0.11%, while Nasdaq-100 futures declined around 1%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures moved in the opposite direction, gaining 0.5%.

The cautious start followed a strong session on Wednesday, when major U.S. indexes closed higher as technology and semiconductor stocks rebounded. The S&P 500 ended 2% higher on Wednesday, while the Nasdaq-100 advanced 1%. The Dow climbed 3% to its highest level in a year. The small-cap Russell 2000 also added 1.6%.

Oil Extends Slide As Geopolitical Risks Ease

Oil prices rebounded in early Thursday trading after initially extending their losses, as investors weighed whether Republicans' setbacks in this week's congressional elections could lower the risk of further escalation in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

Brent crude futures rose around 1.05% to $95.61 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 0.3% to $88.38 as of 3:45 a.m. ET.

The recovery followed a sharp sell-off on Wednesday, when both benchmarks plunged more than 8% to settle at their lowest levels since August 31.

The Tech Radar

Micron Technology (MU): Micron came under pressure in early premarket trading on Thursday, with shares down over 3% as concerns about tighter AI regulation compounded weakness across technology stocks. Democratic Rep. Yassamin Ansari of Arizona called on Wednesday for a pause in advanced AI development until adequate regulations are in place. The prospect of stricter rules has raised concerns that congressional action could slow data center expansion and limit demand for AI computing capacity.

Tesla (TSLA): A potential Tesla-SpaceX merger is facing fresh questions as political pressure on Elon Musk adds to concerns about regulatory hurdles and the value of any takeover premium. Mark Tepper, CEO of Strategic Wealth Partners, raised doubts about the prospects of such a deal, stating that greater scrutiny of Musk could create challenges for both companies. His comments followed Democrats' victories in both chambers of Congress and the Texas governor's race. Texas is home to major Tesla and SpaceX operations, as well as their planned Terafab chipmaking project. Tesla shares had dropped 3% on Wednesday, taking their weekly losses to nearly 4%, and were down 2.2% in early premarket trading on Thursday.

Investing.com — Iceland's Blue Lagoon is showing that high-end, experiential travel is still a draw. The geothermal spa plans to raise €100 million (about $115 million) in a November Nasdaq Iceland listing.

Still, a thinly traded foreign debut brings currency and pricing risk, while Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) is seeing revenue growth slow as city-level rules tighten.

A familiar name, recently marked down, may be the steadier route in. Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG) slid to a 52-week low near $146 on sector jitters, regulatory probes and a trimmed outlook, yet still runs operating margins around 35%.

Data-driven screens are built to spot these mismatches, and ProPicks AI added Booking to its Beat the S&P 500 strategy on November 1. Its November list includes an aerospace propulsion maker up 6.1% in November alone, an analog chip dividend leader up 49.4% since entry and a major health insurer up 15.3% since entry.

See which large-cap leaders the AI picked for November: Explore the Beat the S&P 500 strategy on InvestingPro

Scale and Cash Generation in a Choppy Year

Booking Holdings runs Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable in more than 220 countries and territories. Its third-quarter results on November 3 were mixed. EPS of $4.66 came in 3.8% ahead of consensus and 17% above the $3.98 of a year earlier, and EBITDA rose to $4.61 billion from $4.21 billion. Revenue of $8.9 billion, however, missed estimates by 6.7% and slipped from $9.01 billion a year ago.

Cash returns remain the steadier part of the story. In the second quarter the company returned a record $4.1 billion to shareholders, including $3.7 billion of buybacks, and raised its annual cost-savings target to about $650 million. First-half repurchases totaled $7.4 billion at an average of about $173 a share, trimming the average share count by roughly 6%. Booking's shareholder yield now stands at 8.6%, against 2.3% for its peers. Its Genius loyalty program anchors demand, with Level 2 and 3 members at over 30% of active customers but more than half of room nights.

The sell-off has real triggers. An EU court upheld the block on its $1.9 billion eTraveli deal, Brussels opened a probe into fraudulent listings, the FTC is reportedly preparing action over affiliate ads, and the Middle East conflict led management to trim its full-year outlook. After the third-quarter report, Mizuho cut its target to $205 on margin concerns, and BMO lowered its target to $245 on a softer outlook while keeping an outperform rating.
